Larry F. Taylor, Jr. — The RealLyfe Lawyer

Known as the RealLyfe Lawyer — and as seen on Cochran Law Firm, Texas — Larry has spent nearly two decades taking on hospitals, corporations and insurance companies for families whose lives were changed by someone else's negligence. He personally reviews every case, so you work directly with the attorney, not a nameless intake team.
Built for the cases others walk away from

Birth injury and medical malpractice claims are some of the most complex in law — most firms won't touch them. We do, because these are the cases where the truth matters most. Every claim stands on real medical experts and detailed life-care plans, not guesswork.

Larry F. Taylor, Jr. — @RealLyfeLawyer — is the attorney you'll actually work with. You'll understand what happened to your family and what your options are, not a nameless intake team passing your case around.
Insurers and hospitals settle fairly when they know your lawyer is prepared to try the case. Every claim we build stands on real medical experts and detailed life-care plans — no shortcuts.
You pay nothing up front, and nothing at all unless we recover for you. We Win, You Win — period.

items.q: How much does it cost to hire the RealLyfe Lawyer?
items.a: Nothing up front. We work on contingency — you pay no attorney fee unless we win or settle your case.

items.q: Do you only handle birth injury cases?
items.a: No. Birth injury and medical malpractice are our flagship focus, but we also handle mass torts, traumatic brain injury, car wrecks, truck wrecks and wrongful death across TX, OK, NM & AZ.

items.q: How long do I have to file a claim?
items.a: It depends on your state and case type — often two years, but sometimes less, with special rules for children. Call as soon as possible so we can review the timeline with you.

items.q: How do I know if my baby's injury was caused by negligence?
items.a: Not every difficult birth involves negligence, and not every injury is preventable. A free case review lets us evaluate the medical records against the applicable standard of care.
Yes, in Oklahoma, New Mexico and Arizona. Where required by state law, we work with locally licensed co-counsel.
